key_insight: Droplet projection area provides a geometry-based scaling parameter for predicting impact loads from droplets with non-ideal shapes and orientations.
engineering_relevance: Accounting for droplet morphology could improve wind turbine leading-edge erosion predictions beyond idealized spherical, normal-incidence impacts.
method: Couple incompressible multiphase flow simulations with finite element analysis of blade materials.
Investigate impact dynamics across arbitrary droplet shapes and orientations.
Derive a universal scaling law using initial droplet projection area.
evidence_signal: Simulations show positive correlations among peak pressure, influential area at the pressure peak, and peak force, with peak-force timing scaling inversely; the abstract reports no quantitative errors or experimental validation.
watch_item: The proposed scaling law needs validation across realistic rain conditions and blade materials before use in erosion-life predictions.
paper_title: Influence of Droplet Morphology on Fluid Dynamics and Impact Erosion of Wind Turbine Blades
